summary.headline: Kuantum Papers Q2 FY27 revenue fell 8% QoQ to INR279 crores and PAT was INR2 crores, as PM 3 shutdown and input costs hit a lean quarter.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operational income was INR279 crores, down 8% QoQ, as the PM 3 rebuild (28 June to 21 August 2026) cut volumes by about 6,000 tons. EBITDA was INR35 crores at a 12.4% margin, down 84 bps, on lower realisations and higher raw material and fuel costs linked to the West Asia conflict. PAT was INR2 crores (0.8% margin). H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR533 crores, but H1 PAT was only INR9 crores because depreciation and finance costs rose. Management guided to a 7% to 11% price increase over Q3 and Q4, of which about 4% was taken in late September.

financial_highlights.change: lower due to higher depreciation and finance costs

segments.name: Writing and printing paper (core, four PMs)
segments.commentary: Q2 production was 40,600 tons, with the remaining machines running at 100% utilisation. Management said orders were booked in advance and all output was sold. Specialty paper is about 17% to 18% of the mix, against a target of 25% to 30% in 12 to 15 months.

segments.name: Paperboard / kraft
segments.commentary: Management said a minimum import price (MIP) is already notified for kraft and paperboard varieties. No segment financials were given.

guidance_outlook: Price increases of 7% to 11% targeted by end of year, across Q3 and Q4. About 4% was taken in late September and is being sustained. The next hike is expected after Diwali.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 14%. Management also said industry margins should recover to 18% to 20% in FY28. Analysts' 17% to 18% H2 figure was not confirmed.
Revenue target of over INR1,300 crores for FY27 reiterated. Management said Q3 should be far better than Q2, with lost volume of about 6,000 tons to be regained.
Cost savings of about 1.5% to 2% on total chemical consumption expected from the single-vendor TCM chemical solution.
Depreciation of about INR80 crores per year. Debt repayment of INR180 crores in FY27 is on track, with a similar amount in FY28. Management said deleveraging will begin after the next two years.
Target of about 1 crore clonal saplings a year in the next two to three years. Current production is 17.93 lakh saplings in the quarter.
capex_capacity: PM 3 commissioned 28 August 2026, rebuilt in 59 days against a 65-day plan. All four paper machines are now upgraded, adding a film press, I-table, table vision, web break monitoring, calendaring and automatic starch cooking.

Marketable output is about 600 tons per day at the optimised product mix, against a design capacity of 675 tons per day on an anchor GSM of 64. Orders are shifting to 52 to 58 GSM, which lowers tonnage.
Double Displacement Digester system improved wood pulp yield by 1% and cut steam use from 1.8 to 0.8 metric tons per tonne of pulp.
Environmental projects (lime kiln and CNCG gas handling) are in progress, with about INR139 crores of CWIP, to be completed in Q3 FY27. Management said there is no further major capex planned.
Environmental clearance has been applied for and is at an advanced stage. The 20 MW turbine generator and a 30 TPH boiler were overhauled during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 was seasonally lean and the industry faced cost inflation. Management said Q2 had almost no price increase, with the first hike taken in the last week of September.

Imports have fallen because of higher ocean freight from the Gulf conflict, and exports have also fallen, so domestic supply is more balanced. Anti-dumping duty applications on writing and printing paper are with the government, with 3 to 6 months expected for completion.

Wood (about INR12,000/tonne) is expected to stay flat or fall as availability improves. Wheat straw prices are temporarily elevated after unseasonal rain and a labour shortage, and are expected to normalise after Diwali.

Starch is about 2% to 2.5% of paper cost. Sulphuric acid from West Asia added about 2% to sales cost. Fuel costs rose about 3% to 3.5%. Input coal costs rose about 2.5% to 3%. Coal mix is about 85% coal and 15% agro.
Chinese capacity is being cut (Chenming and Nine Dragons closures), and Indonesian exports are steady.

qa_highlights.question: What is the West Asia war impact on costs, and what was the wood-cost offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphuric acid and chemicals added about 2% to sales cost, and fuel about 3% to 3.5%. Raw material cost and consumption fell 15% to 17% versus Q1, but no absolute figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q2 production loss from the PM 3 shutdown?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6,300 tons lost, mainly from PM 3. Management put the EBITDA impact at about INR40 crores, though the transcript does not say whether this is per tonne or total.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes last, and what H2 margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects hikes to hold for at least two quarters. H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 14%. Analysts cited 17% to 18% for H2, and management did not dispute that figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why has CWIP risen to INR139 crores, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance is for auxiliary efficiency items and environmental projects (lime kiln and CNCG), to be completed in Q3 FY27. Management said no further major capex is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt is about INR700 crores. Depreciation is about INR80 crores a year. Debt repayment is INR180 crores in FY27, with a similar amount in FY28. Deleveraging is expected after the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will capital be returned to shareholders, through buybacks or a higher promoter stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is on cash flow for debt repayment, and there are no plans for changes to the equity capital structure.

risks_watch: Price hikes of 7% to 11% depend on market acceptance and on the anti-dumping decision. Management said the market's acceptance is not unlimited.
Coal supply is constrained because allocated coal is being diverted to the power sector. Open-market coal is available but more expensive.
Mix shift to 52 to 58 GSM is cutting tonnage below the 675 TPD design capacity, and output is now about 600 TPD. Management said it is targeting revenue over tonnage.
Debt of about INR700 crores and higher depreciation and interest will weigh on PAT for the next two years. H1 PAT was INR9 crores.
Watch for environmental clearance, Q3 price realisations, completion of the lime kiln and CNCG projects, and the anti-dumping and MIP outcome for writing and printing paper.
Wheat straw and fuel costs are expected to normalise after Diwali, but management also said input costs are rising structurally.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and the completed modernisation, but cautious on the near term. Management stressed cost pressures, lean-season weakness, and that Q3 price gains depend on market acceptance. Several answers were vague on specifics such as absolute cost figures, and some answers on China and capital allocation were brief.
key_quotes: We are proud to share that with this commissioning, all 4 paper machines have now been successfully upgraded and modernized in line with our mill upgradation plan.
We are expecting prices to increase in the range of 7% to 11%.
So these are only efficiency initiatives, which were defined along the way.
So today, we are at our peak debt level of about INR700 crores. It's only going to improve from here.

rows.label: Anti-dumping duty on writing and printing paper
rows.why: Applications are with government with 3-6 months expected for completion, and it is a key swing factor for the 7-11% price hike; MIP already notified for kraft and paperboard.
